answer:
Done. `analysis.py` runs end-to-end (no args, ~4 s CPU, numpy/scipy/stdlib only) and writes all 12 artifacts. The pipeline: (1) 3-D thin-plate-spline RBF of u(t,x,y) from the 1164 scattered points (t scaled ×12, same scaling at eval), regulariser λ chosen by a seeded 20% holdout CV; (2) |∇u| ridge → exactly two connected front components per time, unit normal n=∇u/|∇u|, signed normal speed v_n=−u_t/|∇u| (central diff interior, one-sided at t_0/t_5); (3) constant-velocity advection u_t+α_x u_x+α_y u_y=0 least-squares fit at the curve points.

KEY DIAGNOSTICS (as requested):
• Reconstruction train RMS = 0.0531 (λ=1e-1, the holdout-CV minimum; holdout RMS 0.161). Reconstructed plateaus at t=0.464: LOW=−1.207 / MID=−0.497 / HIGH=+0.216 (observed −1.25/−0.50/+0.25).
• Fronts: exactly 2 connected components at ALL 6 times (322–364 curve pts each, via |∇u| ridge at frac=0.3). H/M front sits lower-left, L/M front upper-right.
• Per-front mean normal speeds (per evaluation time; [frontA, frontB] = the two components by size):
    t_0 (0.046): [1.22, 2.33]   t_1 (0.130): [1.38, 1.35]   t_2 (0.213): [0.49, 1.65]
    t_3 (0.297): [2.01, −0.01]  t_4 (0.380): [1.23, −0.15]  t_5 (0.464): [2.14, −0.01]
  Overall mean v_n per time: +1.71, +1.35, +1.06, +1.02, +0.60, +1.17. One front advects at ~1–2 throughout; the other slows to ~0 in the second half → differential advection.
• Fitted α_x = −0.6016, α_y = −0.7634 (|v|=0.972, down-left).
• fit_residual_rms = 1.7956; R² = −0.014 → confidence = "low".
• consistency_report: median_residual = 0.999, p90_residual = 2.947, pass_fraction_20pct = 0.079.

HONEST CAVEATS:
1. matplotlib was NOT installed in this environment and could not be installed (no network). I generated reconstruction_slices.png with a self-contained numpy+stdlib(zlib,struct) PNG encoder — a valid 888×668 PNG, 6 panels (viridis field + red curve-point overlay, per-panel t titles). analysis.py therefore runs with only numpy/scipy/stdlib and works with or without matplotlib present (matplotlib is allowed-but-not-required by the constraints).
2. The constant-velocity advection model is a poor pointwise fit (R²≈0, pass_frac≈0.08) because the two fronts advect at different normal speeds; a single velocity captures the direction but not the speed spread. Reported honestly with confidence="low"; per-front level-set transport is listed in model_candidates.json as the better-fitting family.
3. Per-point v_n from −u_t/|∇u| has a heavy tail (up to ~7.8) at band-edge cells where |∇u| is small; the median (~1–2) is robust. Endpoint (t_0,t_5) speeds use one-sided time differences and are noisier (visible in diagnostic_report per-time p90).
